question: A stationary equipment trolley of mass 10 kg is pulled across a rough horizontal concrete floor by an applied horizontal force of 400 N through a displacement of 20.0 m. The coefficient of kinetic friction is μ_k = 0.20. Using the Work-Energy Theorem (W_net = ΔE_k), calculate the final velocity of the trolley (g = 9.8 m·s⁻²):
wrong_answers_pool: 321.60 m·s⁻¹ (forgot to take square root of vf²)
12.68 m·s⁻¹ (omitted factor of 2 in kinetic energy)
explanation: 1. Friction: f_k = μ_k × m × g = 0.20 × 20 × 9.8 = 39.2 N. 2. Net force: F_net = F_app - f_k = 200 - 39.2 = 160.8 N. 3. W_net = F_net × Δx = 160.8 × 20.0 = 3216.0 J. 4. Work-Energy Theorem: W_net = 1/2 × m × vf² => vf = √(2 × W_net / m) = √(2 × 3216.0 / 20) = 17.93 m·s⁻¹.

tags.learning_outcome: Calculate final velocity using work-energy theorem with friction

question: A technical object of mass 0.80 kg travels at a constant velocity of 8.0 m·s⁻¹ eastwards. Calculate its linear momentum:
wrong_answers_pool: 51.20 kg·m·s⁻¹ eastward (used v² instead of v)
25.60 J (calculated kinetic energy instead of momentum)
explanation: Linear momentum: p = m × v = 0.80 kg × 8.0 m·s⁻¹ = 6.40 kg·m·s⁻¹ eastward.
